title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 61
paragraphs: And the third tripod, also in hexameter verse, says:
“Me Laodamas offered to you, fair-aiming Apollo, being king, out of his wealth, as a gift most fair in your honor.”

It was in the reign of this very Laodamas, son of Eteocles, that the Cadmeians were driven out by the Argives and went off to join the Encheleans; and the Gephyraeans, left behind then, were afterwards forced by the Boeotians to withdraw to Athens. Moreover, they have temples established in Athens in which the other Athenians have no part; and among other distinctive shrines, they have especially a temple of Demeter Achaia and a celebration of her mysteries.
